title: Dynamics 365 Unified Routing - Simply Explained

entities.name: Dynamics 365
entities.quote: this knowledge nugget puts Dynamics 365 unified rooting into plain English

quotes.text: A queue only answers part of the question, it can tell you where a request should wait, but it doesn't always decide which available person has the right knowledge, who already handles several chats, or whether a more urgent request should come first.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains precisely why simple queues are not enough for growing service teams.

quotes.text: Your service leaders still decide which customers need faster help, what skills matter, how many chats an agent can manage, and where work should go when nobody matches. Unified routing takes those decisions and applies them the same way each time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes clear that routing automates human service decisions rather than replacing them.

quotes.text: Only add a rule when the information changes where the work goes, who can handle it, or how urgently it needs attention. If a detail doesn't affect routing, it may not belong in a routing rule.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a simple design rule that prevents overcomplicated classification setups.

quotes.text: Push Assignment fits a busy service desk where speed and steady distribution matter. Pick Assignment Fits work where the agent needs more control before accepting the next request.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Contrasts push and pick assignment in one clear decision guideline.

quotes.text: A fallback cue isn't a place to forget difficult work. It's an early warning sign that your planned path needs attention.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the fallback queue as a monitoring signal instead of a dumping ground.

takeaways: Unified routing first classifies incoming work with skills, language and priority, then assigns it to an available agent who has the right skills and free capacity.
Workstreams define the path for each kind of work, queues set team ownership, skills describe fit, and capacity profiles plus presence show who can take work now.
Build queues, people, skills and capacity before routing rules, keep rules minimal, and give the fallback queue an owner who watches it.
hook: Growing service teams quickly find that one shared queue sends urgent cases to the wrong people or leaves them waiting. This episode explains Dynamics 365 unified routing for customer service leads and admins. You learn how workstreams, queues, skills and capacity work together so every request reaches the right agent the first time.
